The graph of the function $f(x),$ which is defined on $[-5,5],$ is shown above. It consists of line segments.

Find the average value ${f}_{\text{avg}}$ of $f(x)$ on $[-4,4].$ Do not round the answer.

${f}_{\text{avg}}=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The average value of a function on a given interval $[a,b]$ is 

$$
{f}_{\text{avg}}=\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Using the additive property of the definite integral, we write

$$
{\int }_{-4}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-4}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{0}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{2}}.
$$

The 1st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-4,0].$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4\cdot 2 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
{\int }_{-4}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{1}=-4.
$$

The 2nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [0,4].$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4\cdot 3 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
{\int }_{0}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{2}=-6.
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-{A}_{1}-{A}_{2} \\  & =-4-6 \\  & =-10.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the formula for the average value, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4-(-4)}\cdot (-10) \\  & =-\frac{10}{8} \\  & =-\frac{5}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
